item.title: Brain May Treat Seizures As Memories
item.description: The brain is a master at learning, but sometimes it learns the wrong things. Scientists find that sleep after a seizure acts as a "save button" for epilepsy.

item.title: Neurons Use RNA “Tentacles” to Survive Starvation
item.description: Researchers discover that neurons pair inactive ribosomes using RNA "tentacles" to save energy and survive during periods of starvation or stress.

item.title: MRI Risk: Nerve Implants Can Trigger Unintended Shocks
item.description: A hidden danger in the magnet. Scientists discover that vagus nerve implants can be "tricked" into firing by MRI fields, causing unintended pain for patients.

item.title: Beyond Fear: Amygdala is the Brain’s Strategic Mediator
item.description: It’s time to retire the "fear center" label. Scientists discover that the amygdala is actually a strategic arbiter that helps the brain navigate complex choices.

item.title: AI Tools Track Every Neuron in Moving Animals
item.description: No more manual labeling. Scientists have unleashed AI to track every single neuron in wriggling animals, turning a five-hour task into a near-instant result.

item.title: Childhood Diet Leaves a Lasting Mark on the Brain
item.description: Childhood junk food leaves a "hidden" mark on the brain. Scientists discover how early diets rewire the hypothalamus and how gut bacteria can help fix it.

item.title: Boosting Mitochondria to Enhance Long-Term Memory
item.description: Overclocking the brain. Scientists discover how to boost mitochondrial energy to turn short-term experiences into long-term memories with just a single session.

item.title: Dopamine Signals Astrocytes to Sculpt the Brain
item.description: Neurons write the draft, but astrocytes edit the circuit. Scientists discover how star-shaped brain cells use dopamine signals to prune synapses and master new motor skills.

item.title: Oxytocin Crash: Why Sleep Loss Leaves You Socially Forgetful
item.description: Forgetful after a late night? Scientists find that sleep loss "mutes" the brain's oxytocin signals, breaking the circuits that help us recognize friends and remember new faces.

item.title: Gut-Brain-Heart Axis: How Microbes Control Your Blood Pressure
item.description: It’s not just in your chest. Scientists discover a "gut-brain-heart axis" where a single bacterial molecule acts as a remote control for your heart's health.
